stem: When explaining posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) epidemiology during evaluation, which anatomic pattern aligns with standard references?

options.text: Often extranodal; may initially involve the gastrointestinal tract, lung, or kidney
PTLD is always confined to cervical lymph nodes only
Extranodal involvement never occurs in transplant recipients
PTLD involves only the transplanted allograft and never other organs

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD is often extranodal and may initially involve the gastrointestinal tract, lung, or kidney, and may involve single or multiple organs.

rationale_incorrect.B: PTLD presentation is variable and may involve multiple extranodal sites beyond cervical nodes alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Extranodal involvement is specifically described rather than being absent.
rationale_incorrect.D: PTLD may involve organs beyond the allograft, including GI tract, lung, or kidney.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 1. Epidemiology → c.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Often extranodal; may initially involve the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, lung, or kidney

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 1.c. (often extranodal; may involve GI tract, lung, or kidney); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Extranodal-site epidemiology angle distinct from single/multiple-organ item (cctc-2133) and nonrenal-incidence item (cctc-3110); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.

stem: When teaching about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) recognition, which lymphatic finding aligns with standard presentation references?

options.text: PTLD presents only with graft tenderness and never with lymph node enlargement
Lymphadenopathy excludes PTLD from the differential

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include lymphadenopathy along with fever, night sweats, and mononucleosis-like symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Lymphadenopathy is specifically listed among PTLD presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: PTLD may present with systemic and nodal findings rather than isolated graft tenderness alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Lymphadenopathy is among cited presentations rather than excluding PTLD.

stem: A liver transplant recipient reports persistent abdominal pain without fever. Which PTLD presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Abdominal pain may be part of PTLD clinical presentation
Abdominal pain always indicates acute rejection and never PTLD
Abdominal pain excludes GI tract involvement in PTLD

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include abdominal pain along with diarrhea, GI tract involvement, and other systemic symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Abdominal pain may reflect PTLD, infection, or other complications and requires clinical evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Abdominal pain and GI involvement are listed among PTLD presentations.
rationale_incorrect.D: Abdominal pain may accompany GI tract PTLD involvement rather than excluding it.

stem: A coordinator is updating PTLD risk-factor teaching for the evaluation team. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: CMV infection is a risk factor for PTLD.
CMV mismatch with a donor CMV-seropositive and recipient CMV-seronegative pair is a risk factor.
Lung and heart-lung transplant types are among higher-risk groups.
Primary Epstein-Barr virus infection has no association with PTLD risk.

explanation.rationale_correct: CMV infection, CMV mismatch, and lung or heart-lung transplant type are cited PTLD risk factors. Statement IV is false because primary EBV infection with donor EBV-seropositive and recipient EBV-seronegative mismatch is a major risk factor.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—lung and heart-lung transplant types are listed among risk factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because primary EBV infection is a key PTLD risk factor.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 2. Risk factors
primary_anchor.quote_hint: CMV infection … CMV mismatch … Type of transplant (lung; heart-lung) … Primary Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 2.b.–e. (primary EBV infection, CMV infection, CMV mismatch, lung/heart-lung type); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
